title: The Shifting Seas: Navigating Global Maritime Trade
subtitle: An examination of how geopolitical tensions and climate change are reshaping the world's most critical shipping lanes.
description: This series explores the complex infrastructure of global maritime trade, which carries over 80% of the world's goods. Readers will gain insight into the historical, economic, and environmental forces currently forcing a rethink of international shipping routes.

articles.label: Part 1
articles.note: Explaining the fundamental importance of maritime chokepoints like the Suez and Panama Canals.

articles.label: Part 2
articles.note: The roles of shipping giants, port authorities, and major naval powers in securing trade routes.

articles.label: Part 3
articles.note: How the Panama Canal drought and Red Sea security crises have forced a permanent shift in thinking.

articles.label: Part 4
articles.note: The impact on consumer prices, manufacturing, and the specific vulnerability of export-dependent economies like Taiwan.

articles.label: Part 5
articles.note: The future of trade routes, including the Arctic passage, digitalization, and the push for greener shipping.
